newsitem.title: NIGERIA: U.S. envoy urges Nigeria to tackle image.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy urges Nigeria to tackle image.

text.p: Nigeria needs to redeem its image abroad to encourage U.S. businesses to invest in the country, the United States ambassador in Lagos said on Wednesday.
Walter Carrington told the business community at American Businessman's Day in Lagos that U.S. businesses were shying away from Nigeria because of the country's "famous image problem".

"There are thousands of U.S. businesses and citizens whose only knowledge of Nigeria is the '419' scam letter they have received. News such as the recent drug bust in Chicago of a ring allegedly led by Nigerian women only reinforces this criminality," he said.
The U.S. two weeks ago smashed a drug ring in the United States believed to be run by Nigerian women.

The African nation has a reputation as the home of advance fee fraud called "419" after a section of the criminal code dealing with fraud in which foreigners are sweet-talked to part with money for deals that turn out to be non-existent.
The United States is Nigeria's single largest trading partner with total American investments of $4 billion, mostly in the oil sector.
Carrington said this was "one of the largest U.S. presences in the world."
But relations between the two have soured since 1993 when the army rulers annulled an election to restore democracy.
Washington is also highly critical of alleged human rights abuses in the country and the slow pace of democratisation by military government.
Carrington said political detentions in Nigeria were still attracting concerns in the United States.
"If political persons are not released soon, that concern is likely to lead to new demands in the in-coming congress (U.S. parliament) for stiffer sanctions," he said.

U.S. sanctions already in place against Nigeria since 1993 and reinforced when nine minority rights activists were hanged last year include a ban on arms sales and no visas to the United States for Nigerian officials and their families.
